thread:
customer_acme: Hi, we started seeing structured JSON responses from /v1/chat_stream get a trailing comma or drop the last field about ~12:03 UTC. Our parser fails with 'Unexpected token } in JSON at position 102'. Request id: req-0a1b2c3d. Happened across a few requests, customer-facing.

maria: Sorry about that — can you paste a raw capture of the stream (no client-side reassembly)? Also which SDK or client are you using? :thinking:

customer_acme: Using our node service. We stream the response and pipe to a JSON stream parser. I'll attach the raw bytes in a sec. It looks like the stream ended with ",\n  \"final_field\": \"value\",\n}" — note the extra comma before the closing brace.

alex: Could be a chunk boundary problem or an abrupt connection close that cut off a partially-written chunk. Any chance there was an auth token rotation mid-request? We've seen some proxies reset keepalives when headers change.

customer_acme: Hmm we do rotate short-lived keys (15m) automatically. I didn't think that would affect an ongoing stream but maybe. How would we confirm?

maria: Can you repro with curl --no-buffer to get raw SSE/chunk output? Example curl:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat_stream?model=..." 
```

Attach the exact bytes you receive (don't let your parser reassemble for you).

customer_acme: Attached raw_dump.txt (first 2 responses). I see a chunk that ends with "...\n  \"final_field\": \"val" then next chunk is "ue\",\n}" but in the failure case the second chunk never arrived — socket closed with FIN. Logs show "RST from 10.2.0.3" near the same time.

eng-oncall: pinging infra — @ops-bot did we have any connection resets or health checks around that time from the load balancer or token service?

ops-bot: load-balancer: brief connection drain detected on worker-17 at 2026-03-14T12:03:09Z; upstream returned 502 on persistent connection. Auth-proxy: rotated keys at 2026-03-14T12:03:00Z. Correlation score 0.72.

samira: That correlation is telling. If the auth-proxy rotated keys and the LB then forced a reconnect, streams in flight could be cut mid-chunk. Structured JSON modes are brittle if the final chunk is missing. We should treat this as a correctness gap — we shouldn't emit partial tokenized JSON that leaves trailing commas.

alex: Short-term mitigation for customers: advise using a tolerant stream-to-object strategy: buffer until a syntactic boundary (closing brace) or use nsq/retry to re-request the trailing delta. Long-term: server should flush full JSON objects per SSE/data event or ensure chunk boundaries don't break tokens.

maria: For support tickets: ask customers to capture raw stream with --no-buffer and send curl logs + request id. We should also run a small repro: simulate the auth-proxy rotation mid-request and see if we can reproduce truncation.

eng-oncall: I'll repro in staging. Plan:
1) Start streaming request from client with token that will rotate in 10s.
2) Have auth-proxy rotate and LB mark worker for drain.
3) Capture bytes and see whether final JSON piece is lost or a partial token remains.

customer_acme: Thanks. If you confirm it's the rotation, any ETA on a fix? We have a user-visible error path.

samira: If confirmed, short fix is to ensure the server writes complete JSON events (no trailing commas) before yield/flush. Longer fix: keep-alive semantics across auth-rotations or graceful draining that lets streams finish. I'll create a JIRA and tag runtime/serving and auth teams.

maria: Also attaching a quick Python repro snippet customers can use to validate locally:

```
import requests
r = requests.get(url, stream=True, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ..."})
for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
    print(repr(chunk))
```

If you see a final chunk that is a partial token (like b'\"val'), that's the bug case.

ops-bot: created incident-3847 with tags [streaming, auth-rotation, structured-json].

alex: Repro in staging is scheduled. Will follow up in this thread with logs and a minimal failing payload. For now, customers: enable retry-on-truncated-stream or buffer until a full JSON object detected.

customer_acme: Great — thanks everyone, looking forward to the follow-up. :pray:
